learn.title: Network connectivity and performance design
objectives: Recommend internet connectivity: Standard public IPs and prefixes, NAT gateway for explicit outbound SNAT, Azure Front Door for global ingress, and Azure DNS public zones and alias records
Choose between public endpoints, service endpoints and private endpoints (Private Link), and design private DNS with Private DNS zones and Azure DNS Private Resolver

Recommend hybrid connectivity: site-to-site and point-to-site VPN, zone-redundant and active-active VPN gateways, ExpressRoute circuits, peerings, SKUs, Global Reach, ExpressRoute Direct and VPN backup
Design the network topology: hub-and-spoke with VNet peering and gateway transit, Azure Virtual WAN, Azure Virtual Network Manager, route tables, user-defined routes and Azure Route Server
Optimise network performance with accelerated networking, proximity placement groups, ExpressRoute FastPath, edge caching in Front Door and Network Watcher diagnostics
concepts: Default outbound access and private subnets

VMs without an explicit outbound method used to get a Microsoft-owned outbound IP that can change. For API versions released after March 31, 2026, subnets in new VNets are private by default, so VMs need an explicit method such as a NAT gateway to reach the internet. Existing VNets aren't changed.
Azure NAT Gateway

Subnet-level outbound-only SNAT using static public IPs or a public IP prefix, with dynamic SNAT port allocation. It takes precedence over load balancer outbound rules and instance public IPs, but a UDR sending 0.0.0.0/0 to an appliance or virtual network gateway overrides it. Standard is zonal; StandardV2 is zone redundant and needs StandardV2 public IPs.
Service endpoint vs private endpoint

A service endpoint extends a subnet's identity to a PaaS service over the Azure backbone, but the service keeps its public IP and it can't be used from on-premises. A private endpoint gives the service instance a private IP in your VNet, reachable from peered VNets and on-premises over VPN or ExpressRoute.
Private DNS for private endpoints

Each private endpoint needs an A record in the matching privatelink zone (for example privatelink.blob.core.windows.net) linked to the VNets that resolve it. In hub-and-spoke, keep the zones central and use Azure Policy to create the DNS records automatically.
Azure DNS Private Resolver

A managed DNS service in your VNet. The inbound endpoint gets a private IP that on-premises DNS servers forward to; the outbound endpoint with a DNS forwarding ruleset sends queries for on-premises domains to on-premises DNS. It replaces DNS forwarder VMs.
VPN Gateway SKUs

Use the zone-redundant AZ SKUs (VpnGw1AZ to VpnGw5AZ) for new gateways; non-AZ SKUs are being migrated. Basic is for dev/test only: no BGP, no active-active, no OpenVPN and no RADIUS. A new VPN gateway needs a Standard SKU public IP.
Point-to-site protocols

OpenVPN works on most platforms and is required for Microsoft Entra ID authentication with the Azure VPN Client. IKEv2 works with native Windows and macOS clients. SSTP is Windows only. Certificate and RADIUS authentication are also available.
ExpressRoute circuit SKUs and peerings

Local gives access to one or two nearby regions with data transfer included and no Global Reach; Standard covers the geopolitical area; Premium adds global VNet access, more routes and more VNet links. Private peering reaches VNets; Microsoft peering reaches Microsoft public services through route filters.
ExpressRoute Global Reach and Direct

Global Reach links two circuits at different peering locations so on-premises sites talk over the Microsoft backbone (Premium on both if they're in different geopolitical regions). ExpressRoute Direct gives dedicated dual 10, 100 or 400 Gbps ports for physical isolation, very large ingestion and MACsec.
Gateway transit and non-transitive peering

VNet peering, including global peering, isn't transitive. Spokes reach each other through a hub appliance with UDRs, Azure Virtual Network Manager direct connectivity, or Virtual WAN. Spokes share the hub's VPN or ExpressRoute gateway when the hub allows gateway transit and the spoke uses remote gateways.
Azure Virtual WAN

Microsoft-managed hubs with built-in routing. Basic supports only site-to-site VPN. Standard adds ExpressRoute, P2S, VNet-to-VNet and hub-to-hub transit, Azure Firewall and NVAs in the hub. You can upgrade Basic to Standard but not back, and a VNet connects to only one hub.
ExpressRoute FastPath

Sends on-premises traffic straight to VMs, bypassing the ExpressRoute gateway in the data path. It needs Ultra Performance, ErGw3AZ or ErGwScale with at least 10 scale units. Peered spoke VNets, UDRs and Private Link over FastPath need ExpressRoute Direct; internal load balancers and PaaS services in spokes still go through the gateway.
comparisons: Service endpoint vs private endpoint vs public endpoint

Public endpoint: reachable from the internet, limited by firewall rules. Service endpoint: free, subnet-scoped access over the backbone, but still a public IP and no on-premises reach. Private endpoint: a private IP per resource and sub-resource, works from peered VNets and on-premises, costs per endpoint and needs private DNS.

Site-to-site VPN is encrypted IPsec over the internet, fast to set up and cheap, but latency varies. ExpressRoute is a private connection through a provider or ExpressRoute Direct with predictable latency and higher bandwidth, but it isn't encrypted by default; add IPsec over private peering or MACsec on Direct if needed.

Customer-managed hub-and-spoke gives full control of the hub VNet, appliances and UDRs and suits a few regions. Virtual WAN gives managed hubs, automatic any-to-any transit, many branches and SD-WAN partner automation with less routing work but less low-level control.

Peering (regional or global) uses the Microsoft backbone with low latency and no gateways, and is the default choice. VNet-to-VNet VPN adds IPsec through gateways, so it is slower and limited by gateway throughput.
NAT gateway vs load balancer outbound rules vs instance public IP

NAT gateway is the recommended outbound method: subnet-wide, dynamic SNAT, up to 16 IPs or a prefix, no inbound. Outbound rules on a Standard load balancer use manual SNAT port allocation. An instance public IP gives one VM both inbound and outbound exposure.
Accelerated networking vs proximity placement group vs FastPath

Accelerated networking (SR-IOV) cuts latency, jitter and CPU use inside each VM. A proximity placement group places VMs physically close to reduce VM-to-VM latency. FastPath removes the ExpressRoute gateway from the on-premises-to-VM data path.
traps: Expecting a service endpoint to make a PaaS service reachable from on-premises; only a private endpoint gives it a private IP that on-premises can use.
Assuming peering is transitive, or that spoke-to-spoke traffic flows through the hub without an appliance, UDRs, Virtual Network Manager direct connectivity or Virtual WAN.
Picking the Basic VPN gateway SKU when the design needs BGP, active-active, OpenVPN or production support.
Choosing ExpressRoute Local when the design also needs Global Reach, or forgetting that Global Reach across geopolitical regions needs Premium on both circuits.
Forgetting that a UDR sending 0.0.0.0/0 to an appliance or virtual network gateway overrides the NAT gateway for internet traffic.
Assuming FastPath covers peered spokes, spoke internal load balancers or private endpoints on a provider circuit; those need ExpressRoute Direct or still use the gateway.
revision: New VNets have private subnets by default: give VMs an explicit outbound method, ideally a NAT gateway.
Need a fixed, allowlistable egress IP range? NAT gateway with a public IP prefix; StandardV2 for zone redundancy.
Private endpoint = private IP + privatelink DNS zone; on-premises forwards the public zone name to the DNS Private Resolver inbound endpoint.
Hybrid resilience: zone-redundant active-active VPN gateways, two ExpressRoute circuits in different peering locations, or VPN as backup to ExpressRoute.
Global Reach = on-premises to on-premises over Microsoft's backbone; Premium = VNets in other geopolitical regions; Local = cheap data transfer to nearby regions.
Hub-and-spoke: hub allows gateway transit, spokes use remote gateways; UDRs to the hub appliance for spoke-to-spoke; Route Server for BGP with NVAs.
Virtual WAN Standard for many branches, P2S, ExpressRoute and any-to-any transit; Basic is site-to-site VPN only.
Performance: accelerated networking, proximity placement groups, FastPath, Front Door caching; measure with Connection monitor and check routes with next hop.

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to the internet
questions.q: A company runs 40 VMs in one subnet. The VMs must reach external update servers on the internet from a fixed public IP address, must not accept inbound connections from the internet, and administrative effort must be minimised. What should you recommend?
opts: Enable a service endpoint on the subnet
Associate a NAT gateway with the subnet
Assign a public IP address to each VM
Create a private endpoint in the subnet
questions.e: A NAT gateway gives a whole subnet outbound-only SNAT through static public IPs, with no per-VM configuration.

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to the internet
questions.q: On-premises servers connect to Azure over ExpressRoute private peering. They must reach an Azure Storage account by using a private IP address, without traffic crossing the internet. What should you recommend?
opts: Microsoft peering on the ExpressRoute circuit
A service endpoint for Microsoft.Storage
A storage firewall rule for the on-premises IPs
A private endpoint for the storage account

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to on-premises networks
questions.q: Eight developers work from home and need encrypted access to VMs in an Azure VNet from their laptops. The company has no on-premises VPN device and wants to minimise cost. What should you recommend?
opts: A site-to-site VPN to each home router
Global VNet peering to each laptop
A point-to-site VPN on a VPN gateway
An ExpressRoute circuit with private peering

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to on-premises networks
questions.q: A hub VNet has a VPN gateway connected to on-premises. A peered spoke VNet must use that gateway instead of deploying its own. How should you configure the peering?
opts: Use remote gateways on the hub and allow gateway transit on the spoke
Deploy a second VPN gateway in the spoke and connect the two
Allow forwarded traffic on both sides with no gateway settings
Allow gateway transit on the hub and use remote gateways on the spoke
questions.e: Gateway transit is enabled on the peering from the VNet that owns the gateway; the spoke side is set to use the remote gateway.

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network performance
questions.q: A 1 Gbps ExpressRoute provider circuit is saturated. The company needs 2 Gbps, wants to keep the same circuit and can't accept downtime. What should you recommend?
opts: Delete the circuit and create a new 2 Gbps circuit
Add a second VNet peering between the hub and the spokes
Increase the circuit's bandwidth in place, after confirming that the provider's port supports the higher speed
Replace the ExpressRoute gateway with a Basic VPN gateway
questions.e: ExpressRoute circuit bandwidth can be increased without disruption if the provider supports it. It can't be decreased in place.

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network performance
questions.q: Network-intensive VMs show high CPU use from packet processing and variable latency. You must improve network performance without changing the application. Which feature should you enable on supported VM sizes?
opts: IP forwarding on the network interface
A Standard SKU public IP address
Azure Monitor Agent network counters
Accelerated networking
questions.e: Accelerated networking uses SR-IOV to bypass the host virtual switch, lowering latency, jitter and CPU use.

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to the internet
questions.q: A company bought the domain fabrikam.com from a third-party registrar. It wants to manage the public DNS records in Azure with Azure RBAC and activity logs. What should you recommend?
opts: Transfer the domain registration into Microsoft Entra ID
Create an Azure DNS public zone and update the NS records at the registrar
Deploy DNS Private Resolver with an inbound endpoint
Create an Azure Private DNS zone and link it to every VNet

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to on-premises networks
questions.q: A manufacturer needs a connection between its data centre and Azure that doesn't traverse the public internet and offers predictable latency for large daily transfers. What should you recommend?
opts: ExpressRoute
Point-to-site VPN
Azure Front Door
Site-to-site VPN

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to the internet
questions.q: VMs in three VNets must resolve each other by host name under the internal domain corp.contoso.net, and records must be created automatically when VMs are deployed. Administrative effort must be minimised. What should you recommend?
opts: DNS server VMs in each VNet with zone transfers
Hosts files distributed by Azure Policy guest configuration
An Azure Private DNS zone with autoregistration on the VNet links
An Azure DNS public zone with alias records

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network performance
questions.q: After a route table change, traffic from a VM to an on-premises subnet no longer arrives. You need to see which next hop Azure uses for that destination from the VM. Which Network Watcher tool should you use?
opts: Next hop
Traffic analytics
Packet capture
Connection monitor

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to the internet
questions.q: A web app is published through Azure Front Door. Users must reach it at contoso.com (the zone apex) as well as www.contoso.com, and DNS is hosted in Azure DNS. What should you recommend for the apex?
opts: An NS record that delegates the apex to Front Door
A CNAME record at the apex that points to Front Door
An A record with the current Front Door IP address
An alias record set that points to the Front Door endpoint
questions.e: A CNAME isn't allowed at the zone apex; an Azure DNS alias record can point the apex at an Azure resource such as Front Door.

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to the internet
questions.q: A team deploys Windows VMs into a VNet created this month by using the current ARM API version. The VMs have no public IPs or load balancer, and Windows activation and updates fail. Older VNets work fine. What should you recommend?
opts: Link a Private DNS zone to the new VNet
Enable accelerated networking on the VMs
Add an explicit outbound method such as a NAT gateway
Peer the new VNet with an older VNet
questions.e: Subnets in new VNets are private by default, so VMs get no default outbound access and need an explicit outbound method.

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to the internet
questions.q: VMs are spread across three availability zones. Their outbound internet traffic must use static IPs, survive the loss of any one zone and support IPv6, with a single outbound resource to manage. What should you recommend?
opts: A Standard NAT gateway in each zone on one subnet
A Standard NAT gateway pinned to zone 1
Instance-level public IPs on every VM
A StandardV2 NAT gateway with StandardV2 public IPs
questions.e: StandardV2 NAT gateway is zone redundant and supports IPv6; a subnet can have only one NAT gateway.

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to the internet
questions.q: An App Service web app calls a third-party API that accepts requests only from one static IP address that your company controls. What should you recommend?
opts: Integrate the app with a VNet subnet that has a NAT gateway
Add a private endpoint for the web app
Use the app's shared outbound IP address list
Assign a Standard public IP directly to the app
questions.e: With VNet integration routing outbound traffic, the app egresses through the subnet's NAT gateway public IP.

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to the internet
questions.q: You create a private endpoint for a storage account blob service, but VMs in the VNet still resolve the account name to its public IP. The VNet uses Azure-provided DNS. What should you do?
opts: Enable autoregistration on a Private DNS zone for the VNet
Link a privatelink.blob.core.windows.net Private DNS zone with the endpoint record to the VNet
Create a public DNS zone for blob.core.windows.net in Azure DNS
Add a service endpoint for Microsoft.Storage to the subnet

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to on-premises networks

A DNS Private Resolver inbound endpoint as the target of on-premises conditional forwarders

The ExpressRoute Premium add-on

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to on-premises networks
questions.q: Data centres in London and Amsterdam each have an ExpressRoute circuit at a different peering location. Traffic between the two data centres must use the Microsoft backbone without new carrier links. What should you recommend?

questions.t: Bulk transfer to a nearby region

questions.q: A media company sends hundreds of terabytes a month from its data centre to one Azure region in the same metro as an ExpressRoute peering location. It must minimise data transfer cost and doesn't need other regions or Global Reach. Which circuit SKU should you recommend?

ExpressRoute Standard with unlimited data and Premium
ExpressRoute Local

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to on-premises networks
questions.q: A company wants on-premises systems to reach the public endpoints of Azure services in its region over its existing ExpressRoute circuit instead of the internet, advertising only the services it uses. What should you recommend?

Microsoft peering with a route filter for the required services
Private endpoints for every service in a hub VNet
Private peering with a route table for the services

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to on-premises networks
questions.q: In a customer-managed hub-and-spoke network, traffic between two spokes must pass through a network virtual appliance in the hub. Both spokes are peered only to the hub. What should you recommend?

Gateway transit enabled on both spoke peerings
A NAT gateway on the hub appliance subnet
UDRs in each spoke that send the other spoke's prefix to the appliance IP

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to on-premises networks
questions.q: An SD-WAN appliance in a hub VNet must exchange routes dynamically with Azure by using BGP, so that VNet routes and branch routes update without manual UDRs. What should you recommend?
opts: A DNS Private Resolver outbound endpoint
A route table with BGP propagation enabled
Azure Route Server in the hub
Azure Virtual Network Manager mesh

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network performance
questions.q: VNets in East US and West Europe must exchange large volumes of data with the lowest latency and highest throughput, without managing gateways. What should you recommend?
opts: Global VNet peering
ExpressRoute Global Reach
Site-to-site VPN through on-premises
VNet-to-VNet VPN between gateways

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network performance
questions.q: On-premises traffic to VMs in a hub VNet over ExpressRoute is limited by the ExpressRoute gateway, and latency must drop. The gateway is ErGw3AZ. What should you recommend?
opts: Replace the circuit with site-to-site VPN
Add a NAT gateway to the GatewaySubnet
Enable FastPath on the ExpressRoute connection
Enable the ExpressRoute Premium add-on
questions.e: FastPath sends traffic directly to VMs, bypassing the gateway in the data path; ErGw3AZ supports it.

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network performance
questions.q: Traffic between a VM's public IP and internet users must stay on Microsoft's global network for as long as possible to improve performance. Which setting should you choose for the public IP?
opts: Accelerated networking on the VM's NIC
Routing preference set to Microsoft network
A Basic SKU public IP address
Routing preference set to Internet
questions.e: The Microsoft network option uses Microsoft's backbone and is the default; the Internet option hands traffic to ISP networks sooner to reduce cost.

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network performance
questions.q: The network team must continuously measure latency and packet loss from on-premises servers and Azure VMs to an application endpoint, and get alerts when thresholds are breached. Which Network Watcher feature should you use?
opts: Packet capture
IP flow verify
Next hop
Connection monitor

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network performance
questions.q: A site-to-site VPN tunnel is using DES3 and SHA256 and can't reach the throughput the gateway SKU is rated for. You want the best per-tunnel performance without changing the SKU. What should you recommend?
opts: A custom IPsec policy that uses GCMAES256
Switching the tunnel from IKEv2 to IKEv1
A custom IPsec policy that uses AES256 and SHA256
Enabling accelerated networking on the gateway
questions.e: Microsoft's tests show the best throughput with GCMAES256 for both IPsec encryption and integrity.

Azure Virtual Network Manager connectivity configurations

questions.q: Consider these statements: 1) Accelerated networking reduces latency and CPU use by bypassing the host virtual switch. 2) It's available only on VMs that have a public IP address. 3) Enabling it on an existing VM requires the VM to be stopped and deallocated. Which statements are true?
opts: Statements 2 and 3 only
Statement 1 only
Statements 1 and 2 only

questions.t: Public IP SKU for new deployments
questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to the internet
questions.q: You are designing a new internet-facing workload in a region with availability zones. Which public IP configuration should you recommend for its frontend?
opts: A Standard SKU static public IP that is zone redundant
A Basic SKU static public IP in one zone
A Standard SKU public IP pinned to one zone
A Basic SKU dynamic public IP
questions.e: Basic SKU public IPs are retired; Standard public IPs are static and can be zone redundant.

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to on-premises networks
questions.q: A bank's only connection to Azure is one ExpressRoute circuit at one peering location. A regulator requires that a failure of an entire peering location must not interrupt private connectivity at full bandwidth. What should you recommend?
opts: A site-to-site VPN as the only backup path
The Premium add-on on the existing circuit
A second ExpressRoute circuit at a different peering location

questions.e: A circuit already has two links at one location; surviving the loss of a location needs a circuit at another location.

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to on-premises networks
questions.q: An Azure VPN gateway is active-active, and on-premises has two VPN devices. The design must survive the loss of either Azure instance or either on-premises device with automatic failover. What should you recommend?
opts: One tunnel per device to the first instance only
Four tunnels between both instances and both devices, with BGP
Two static-route tunnels from one device to each instance
Two policy-based tunnels with no BGP
questions.e: Dual-redundancy connects each on-premises device to both gateway instances, and BGP is needed to route across the tunnels.

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to on-premises networks
questions.q: A company deployed a Basic Virtual WAN for 20 site-to-site branches. It now needs ExpressRoute, point-to-site users and VNet-to-VNet transit through the hub. What should you recommend?
opts: Add an ExpressRoute gateway to the Basic hub
Create a second Basic Virtual WAN for the new needs
Upgrade the Virtual WAN to Standard
Deploy a VPN gateway in each spoke VNet
questions.e: Basic Virtual WAN supports only site-to-site VPN. The upgrade to Standard is one-way.

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to on-premises networks
questions.q: A spoke subnet has a UDR for 10.0.0.0/16 with next hop a hub firewall. The ExpressRoute gateway also propagates a BGP route for 10.0.1.0/24 to the subnet. Where does traffic to 10.0.1.5 go?
opts: To the ExpressRoute gateway, because 10.0.1.0/24 is the longer prefix
To the firewall, because UDRs always beat BGP routes
It's dropped because the two routes overlap
To the firewall, because 10.0.0.0/16 was created first
questions.e: Azure picks the longest prefix match first; only for identical prefixes does a UDR beat a BGP route.

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to on-premises networks

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network performance
questions.q: A provider ExpressRoute circuit connects to an Ultra Performance gateway in a hub with FastPath enabled. Traffic to VMs in the hub bypasses the gateway, but traffic to VMs in peered spokes in the same region still goes through it. What would let spoke traffic use FastPath?
opts: Enabling the ExpressRoute Premium add-on
Enabling gateway transit on the spoke peerings
Upgrading the gateway to ErGw3AZ
Moving the connection to an ExpressRoute Direct circuit

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to the internet
questions.q: A subnet has a NAT gateway, but a UDR for 0.0.0.0/0 with next hop virtual network gateway was later added for forced tunnelling. Internet traffic from the subnet now leaves through on-premises. Why?
opts: A UDR to a virtual network gateway overrides the NAT gateway
The NAT gateway needs a public IP prefix to take priority
The NAT gateway applies only to inbound traffic
NAT gateways can't be used in subnets with route tables
questions.e: Precedence is UDR to an appliance or gateway, then NAT gateway, then instance public IP, then load balancer outbound rules.

questions.on: Recommend a connectivity solution that connects Azure resources to on-premises networks
questions.q: A healthcare company uses a 1 Gbps provider ExpressRoute circuit with private peering. A new policy requires all traffic between on-premises and Azure VNets to be encrypted, without using the internet. What should you recommend?

MACsec on the provider circuit
A point-to-site VPN for each server
An IPsec site-to-site VPN over ExpressRoute private peering
